newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed in trading lull.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed in trading lull.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were mixed at the close after the market drifted without leads due to a virtual absence of demand, traders said.
The only interest for the day was provided by inquiries on some SMR grades from Far East consumers, which also did not result in business, the traders said.
"They were only asking if we had the (SMR) 20 and what not" said a trader. "They were not even bothered to ask the price."
Business in December was usually slow, with the Christmas and New Year diverting players' attention, traders said.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted January RSS1 buyer at 317.50 ($1.26) a kilogram, down half cent from Tuesday's close. January SMR 20 buyer was quoted half cent higher at 309 cents.
Dealers quoted the SMR CV at 362 cents, SMR L at 343, SMR 5 at 318, SMR 10 at 308, SMR 20 at 307 and drum latex at 236.
The INRO five-day moving average rose to 242.18 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 17 from 241.45 on Dec 16. The daily indicator price jumped to 243.87 from 243.71.
